prompt: When the temperature of the entire universe was between 0 and 100 degrees Celsius, what fraction of the size of the universe was the size of the universe now?
judge_reasoning: The prompt asks for the fraction of the universe’s size now when the universe’s temperature was between 0 and 100°C, which requires mapping temperature to the cosmological scale factor and computing a numerical range. Candidate 1 is the only one that directly provides a fraction and lands in the right order of magnitude (~1%); however, it is not derived cleanly and includes several dubious details. Candidates 2 and 3 do not answer the requested temperature range (3 uses 1000°C; 2 discusses unrelated high-temperature eras), and Candidate 4 misidentifies the relevant epoch for 100°C and omits the required fraction calculation.
